answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond, then slash it when independently sampled work fails verification or colludes in a detected fraud. A Sybil attacker must lock real capital in every identity, so multiplying hollow accounts across a ridge of cheap compute does not multiply influence for free; the bond also makes large-scale attacks costly to sustain. Honest agents recover their stake, while the protocol can use forfeitures to compensate victims or fund audits on the terrace of shared services.
